standards.title: Patients and families are told about their rights
elements: A written patient rights statement is displayed at registration and in each ward in English and Arabic.
Patients receive a copy of their rights on admission and staff record that it was explained.
Staff can describe three patient rights and where the statement is posted.

standards.title: Consent is obtained before treatment
elements: A consent policy defines which procedures need written consent and who may obtain it.
Consent forms in the sampled records are signed, dated and name the procedure in plain language.
Interpreters are used and recorded when the patient does not speak the language of the clinician.

standards.title: Complaints are received, answered and learned from
elements: A complaints procedure sets response times and is available to patients in both languages.
Every complaint in the last quarter was acknowledged within one working day.
Complaint themes are reviewed by the quality committee at least quarterly.

standards.title: Every patient has an assessment on admission
elements: A nursing and medical assessment is completed within the timeframe set by policy.
A falls and pressure injury risk assessment is recorded in all sampled admission records.
Pain is assessed and reassessed with a validated scale.

standards.title: Care is planned and reviewed
elements: A written care plan is present within 24 hours of admission and updated after each review.
Multidisciplinary review of inpatients longer than five days is documented.
Patients and families take part in care planning and this is recorded.

standards.title: Discharge and transfer are planned
elements: Discharge instructions are written in a language the patient understands.
Follow-up appointments and medicines at discharge are reconciled and recorded.
Transfers to other facilities include a handover summary signed by both teams.

standards.title: Medicines are stored safely
elements: High-alert and look-alike medicines are separated and labelled in all storage areas.
Medicine fridges are checked daily with temperature logs for the last 90 days.
Controlled drugs are stored under double lock and counted at each handover.

standards.title: Prescribing and administration follow safe processes
elements: Allergies are recorded on the chart and on a wristband before any medicine is given.
Two nurses independently check high-alert infusions before administration.
Administration is recorded at the time of giving in all sampled charts.

standards.title: Medication errors are reported and reviewed
elements: Staff know how to report a medication error or near miss and do so without blame.
Medication incidents are reviewed monthly with actions tracked to completion.
Pharmacists review high-risk prescriptions within one working day.

standards.title: Hand hygiene is practised and measured
elements: Alcohol hand rub is available at every bed and is checked as full on daily rounds.
Monthly hand hygiene audits cover every ward and results are fed back to staff.
Compliance at or above the target is reached in at least four of the last six months.

standards.title: Equipment is cleaned and sterilised correctly
elements: Sterilisation indicators and load records are kept for every cycle.
Reusable equipment is cleaned between patients according to a written schedule.
Environmental cleaning audits are completed monthly with results reviewed.

standards.title: Infections are monitored and outbreaks are managed
elements: Healthcare-associated infections are counted and reported monthly with a defined denominator.
An isolation policy covers airborne, droplet and contact precautions with clear signage.
An outbreak plan has been tested with a drill in the last 12 months.

standards.title: Quality is planned and measured
elements: A written quality plan sets priorities and is approved by leadership each year.
Indicators have definitions, numerators, denominators and targets in a dictionary.
Indicator results are reviewed by the quality committee every month.

standards.title: Incidents are reported and investigated
elements: Staff can report incidents in under two minutes, including anonymously.
Serious events are investigated with a root cause analysis completed within the deadline.
Corrective actions have an owner, a due date and an effectiveness check.

standards.title: Patient feedback is used to improve care
elements: Patient feedback is collected after discharge and analysed for themes.
Patients who are unhappy receive a call-back and the outcome is recorded.
Improvements made after feedback are shared with staff and patients.

standards.title: The building is safe for patients and staff
elements: A fire safety plan is in place and evacuation drills are held at least twice a year.
Emergency exits are marked, unobstructed and checked weekly.
A risk assessment of the premises is reviewed annually.

standards.title: Medical equipment is maintained
elements: An inventory of medical equipment records service dates and next due dates.
Defibrillators and resuscitation trolleys are checked daily with expiry dates.
Faulty equipment is tagged, removed from use and logged the same day.

standards.title: Utilities and hazardous materials are managed
elements: Backup power is tested monthly and the results are recorded.
Clinical waste is segregated, labelled and collected on a documented schedule.
Hazardous chemicals have safety data sheets available at the point of use.

standards.title: Leaders set direction and are accountable
elements: The organisation has a mission, vision and values that are known by staff.
The governing body approves the budget and the annual quality and safety plan.
Roles and reporting lines are documented in an organisation chart reviewed each year.

standards.title: Policies are controlled
elements: A document control procedure sets version, owner and review date on every policy.
No policy in the sampled set is past its review date.
Staff can find current policies on the intranet or in the ward folder.

standards.title: Ethical issues are handled openly
elements: A code of conduct and a conflict of interest process are in place.
An ethics committee or advisor is available and meets when needed.
Staff can raise concerns confidentially and are protected from retaliation.

standards.title: Staff are qualified and credentialed
elements: Licences and qualifications are verified at recruitment and tracked to renewal.
Clinical privileges for doctors are approved and reviewed on a fixed cycle.
Personnel files in the sample contain verified credentials and a job description.

standards.title: Staff are oriented and trained
elements: All new staff complete orientation including safety, infection control and fire within 30 days.
Basic life support training is current for all clinical staff.
Annual mandatory training completion is monitored and reported by department.

standards.title: Staff performance and wellbeing are supported
elements: Annual appraisals are completed for at least 90 percent of staff.
Staff can report needle-stick and workplace injuries and receive follow-up.
Staffing levels are reviewed against patient need on each ward every month.
